reason: Pedicels can be ascending (held up at an angle); the examples are correct.
Growth habit: a whole plant can be procumbent or trailing.
Pinnae are sessile, subsessile or stalked, which is attachment. 'with stalk 0.5-1 cm' is a stalk length, but the pair is still fine.
A pedicel can be straight or curved.
Lithocysts, the cells that hold cystoliths, can be present or absent. The examples are about cystoliths, which sit inside the lithocyst, so the reading is acceptable.
A lamina can be spatulate.
A leaf lobe can be lanceolate.
A pedicel can be curved, often in fruit. 'curved trichomes' is a different bearer, but the other examples fit.
A pinna has a 2-D shape (ovate, oblong, deltate). Some examples ('base rounded to cuneate') belong to the pinna base, which is a separate part.
A lamina can be scaly, for example with peltate scales (ferns, Elaeagnaceae).
An indumentum (hair or scale covering) can be present or absent. Its content (scales, hairs) belongs to other statements.
A bracteole can be filiform (thread-like).
A capsule can be curved.
Pedicels can be recurved, often in fruit.

Apiculate fits sharpness of a lip apex, but 'retuse' and 'acute' are apex shapes and the part in the examples is the apex, not the lip. A rule would need to send apex shapes to an apex or shape quality and keep only apiculate here.
Auricles have a length. The examples are measurements.
Lateral veins can be inconspicuous (indistinct, obscure).
The adaxial leaf surface has a colour.
A floral disc has a colour. Some examples are about lamellae or stripes on it, which is acceptable.
Veins and veinlets can be inconspicuous or obscure.
A leaf lobe can have an entire margin. Some examples say 'margins entire', which is the margin, but it is the lobe in context.
Secondary veins can be curved or arcuate.
A lamina, usually its base, can be auriculate. Negations ('not auriculate') are handled by the negation rule.

The examples are about veins, nerves and venation being raised, not the lamina. It is correct only if the statement is moved to the vein. A rule would map 'nerves/veins/venation raised' to the vein bearer.
Trichomes have a length, and the examples are measurements.
An achene can be sessile or stipitate, which is attachment.
Pedicels can be present or absent. 'pedunculate' is a peduncle statement, but the main reading is fine.
A panicle can be terminal or axillary.
An involucral bract can be pubescent. This is common in Asteraceae.
A lamina can be hispid (stiff hairs).
A raceme can be terminal, axillary or lateral.
A rhizome can grow ascending.
Cells can be rectangular, as in bryophyte leaf cells.
A corolla lip can be oblong. An orchid lip is a different part, but the shape is still valid.
The abaxial leaf surface has a colour.
A floral disc has a height, and the examples are measurements.
Trichomes and scales have a colour.
A gynostemium (column) has a colour.
A floral disc can be glabrous or hairy.
A lamina, usually its base, can be symmetric or asymmetric.
A corolla lip can be recurved. Some examples are about the apex or tip, but they are acceptable.
'Pale' maps to low saturation, and a lamina can be pale, mostly abaxially.
A leaf has a length-to-width ratio. Some examples are about ligules, which is a different part.
Parallel venation is a leaf trait. 'Margins becoming parallel' is a shape, not venation, so it needs a rule.
Ovules can be present or absent, and counts per locule are acceptable.
A seta can be straight or curved.
Veins can be prominent.
A flower fascicle can be present. The examples only state that it exists.
Stems can be annual, which is life span.
A floral disc can be lobed.
An inflorescence can be subglobose.
An anther locule count (1- or 2-locular) is an amount.
Fronds can be dimorphic (sterile and fertile), which is morphology.
An achene can be biconvex (lenticular).
Spores have a length, and the examples are measurements.
Lateral veins can be curved or arcuate.
A midvein can be conspicuous or distinct.
A bulb has a width, and the examples are measurements.
An involucral bract can be glandular.
A leaf base can be cordate (heart-shaped).
